title: Niki Lauda's birth chart
metaDescription: Niki Lauda's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 3.5° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a opposition: the Sun and Saturn within 0.8°, identity wired to structure. Oppositions are read as full-moon geometry — maximum visibility between two needs that share one spine.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 3.5° Pisces — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by Jupiter. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Pisces and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 7.4° Aquarius, Venus was at 20.1° Aquarius, Mars was at 8.5° Pisces. Read together: a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste led by wit and proportion; drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Neptune a sixth of the circle apart from Pluto, 0.1° off exact. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, the Sun opposition Saturn at 0.8°, and the Sun conjunction Mars at 5.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Jupiter stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, one sits in a sign it has an opinion about. Jupiter in Capricorn at 22.0° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 air, 2 water, 2 earth, 1 fire by element and 4 mutable, 3 fixed, 2 cardinal by modality. An air-weighted chart thinks in through-lines; the sentence is how it takes hold of the world. Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Sagittarius into Capricorn during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.7° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
